label: time-critical illness, cheap and safe response
miss_profile: the patient deteriorates within hours, and the window to act closes fast
response_profile: little more than staff time -- bloods, a scan, fluids, or an early drug dose
pick_if: missing this for a few hours changes the outcome, and acting on a patient who turns out to be well costs you a test and some clinician time, not harm
examples: ED sepsis alert -> lactate, cultures, fluids, empiric antibiotics
suspected pulmonary embolism -> D-dimer or CT pulmonary angiogram
possible ACS in chest pain -> troponin and serial ECG
stroke code activation -> urgent imaging and specialist review
deterioration or early-warning-score alert -> rapid response team review
not_this_tier_if: the response itself is invasive or risky (that is Tier C), or the illness unfolds over days rather than hours (Tier B)
anchor: Pulmonary embolism testing threshold ~1.8-2% (Pauker-Kassirer method); the ED sepsis literature cost build in this framework lands at pt ~6.25%, i.e. R=15

label: serious but not hour-critical, moderate response
miss_profile: the patient gets worse over days -- an avoidable admission, organ injury, or a readmission -- but a few hours either way is not decisive
response_profile: a real but bounded commitment -- a drug course, extra monitoring, an observation bed, or a specialist referral
pick_if: you would be uncomfortable missing it, but you would also not want to start treatment in ten well patients to catch one case
examples: COPD exacerbation -> bronchodilator or steroid course
community-acquired pneumonia -> antibiotics and blood cultures
AKI risk flag -> repeat creatinine, fluid review, nephrotoxin hold
statin or antihypertensive initiation from a risk score
not_this_tier_if: hours matter and the workup is cheap (Tier A), or acting means a procedure with its own complication rate (Tier C)
anchor: Statin primary prevention at 7.5% 10-year ASCVD risk (2018 ACC/AHA guideline)

label: not time-critical, invasive or expensive response
miss_profile: important, but slow-moving -- a delay of days to weeks is usually recoverable because the next visit or test will catch it
response_profile: something with its own risk or a large cost -- a biopsy, an operation, an ICU bed, or long-term therapy the patient may not need
pick_if: acting on a well patient does real harm, so you want reasonable confidence before pulling the trigger
examples: prostate or breast biopsy after a risk calculator
ICU transfer or step-up from a deterioration score
elective surgical referral from a screening pathway
genetic or specialist workup with a long, costly tail
not_this_tier_if: the response is a cheap test rather than a procedure -- that is Tier A or B even when the underlying disease is serious
anchor: Prostate biopsy decision curves commonly evaluate 10-30%; this tier prespecifies 20-30%
